 Haze in Malaysia forced the government to close schools for two days, except in three states. The Head of Bakom RI, Syahganda Nainggolan, urged the former Malaysian Minister of Finance not to seek compensation from Indonesia for losses incurred due to forest and land fire haze. (AP) 
 Writer Adhyasta Dirgantara | Editor Bilal Ramadhan 
 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - The Head of the Indonesian Government Communication Agency (Bakom), Syahganda Nainggolan, urged the former Malaysian Minister of Finance not to seek compensation from Indonesia for the losses incurred due to the haze from forest and land fires (karhutla).
 Syahganda referenced President Prabowo Subianto 's direct apology to Singapore and Malaysia regarding the haze issue.
 "We must recognize that our President has already apologized to Malaysia and Singapore for the recent haze. However, we must reiterate that once the haze ceases, we send oxygen," Syahganda stated at the DPR Building in Senayan, Jakarta, on Thursday (19/11/2026).
 He explained that after Prabowo's apology, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong immediately expressed appreciation towards Indonesia.
 Syahganda called on Malaysia to emulate the graciousness shown by Singapore regarding the karhutla situation in Indonesia.
 "What we need to assure is that after the apology, we observed the response from Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, who expressed appreciation to our President and his entire team from the Republic of Indonesia for their hard work in extinguishing the karhutla fires," he said.
 "So actually, Malaysia should just imitate how Singapore's Prime Minister appreciated the efforts and not ask for compensation," Syahganda added.
 Previously, former Malaysian Finance Minister Lim Guan Eng urged Indonesia to provide compensation for the economic and welfare losses his country suffered due to the haze crisis this year.
 The total loss was estimated to reach 13 billion ringgit, or approximately Rp 57 trillion.
 If Indonesia is unwilling to provide compensation, Lim proposed the establishment of a permanent cross-border task force with authority to enter forests in Indonesia to manage forest fires.
 Lim claimed Malaysia faced welfare losses of 8 billion ringgit and economic losses of 5 billion ringgit due to the haze.
 According to a report by Malay Mail, cited by the South China Morning Post on Wednesday (18/11/2026), these figures come from a study conducted by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM).
 The welfare loss is related to health impacts caused by the haze, encompassing the economic costs from premature mortality risks.
 Lim stated that this impact is linked to an estimated 1,700 premature deaths among Malaysian citizens.
 Meanwhile, the economic loss of 5 billion ringgit (around Rp 22 trillion) is based on economists' estimates that severe air pollution could reduce the number of international tourist arrivals by up to 8 percent.
 This decline is expected to cause losses of up to 5 billion ringgit for the tourism sector's gross domestic product (GDP) and its downstream economic effects.
 Lim considers this situation a threat to the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign that the Malaysian government is currently promoting.
